messages:
Luis: Hey team — our nightly embeddings job started hitting 429s around 03:10 UTC. It was a bulk run: ~75k docs, batch size 512, ~30 concurrent workers. We were at ~30k completions/min when it started failing. Getting a ton of `429` with Retry-After sometimes, sometimes not. Can someone help triage?

Anna (support): Sorry you're seeing this, Luis. Do you have a sample response payload for a 429? Also which API key / project? We can check per-key rate buckets.

Luis: Pasting one response — headers scrubbed:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1852001300
Retry-After: 7
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "burst limit exceeded for embeddings.requests"
}
```

Mike (infra): Hmm, X-RateLimit-Limit of 60k looks like a per-minute bucket for that key but Remaining 0 indicates you hit it. That reset timestamp is 1852001300 (about 66s after the root). Looks like we throttled the burst window. Are you sure all workers share the same API key?

Luis: Yes, single API key across the job. Our job spins 30 processes from the same CI host.

Julie (eng-sre): Quick note on how bursts work: we have a short-term burst window plus a longer sustained window. If you push many concurrent requests that complete quickly, the short window can be used up and you'll see 429s even though long-term average might be OK. The Retry-After header is advisory — clients should do exponential backoff with jitter.

Anna (support): Two immediate mitigations: throttle concurrency on your side (reduce workers to 6–8) and add exponential backoff honoring Retry-After. Also try smoothing bursts by staggering job start times across workers.

Luis: Any guidance for patching the job? We're aiming to keep overall elapsed time low.

Julie (eng-sre): Recommendations we've seen work: 1) increase batch size a bit (fewer requests) but careful with memory and model limits; 2) reduce parallel connections to the API key (concurrency limit per key); 3) implement per-key token bucket locally to pace requests; 4) request a Dedicated capacity if you need sustained high QPS.

Mike (infra): You can also space the workers using a random jitter at spawn time: sleep(random.uniform(0, 0.5)) before each worker starts to avoid synchronized bursts. For immediate repro: run 50 concurrent curl requests sending 512-item batches and you should see 429s quickly.

Luis: We saw a weird pattern — some 429s had Retry-After header, some just returned the 429 body with no Retry-After. Is that expected?

Anna (support): It can happen when the violation is detected at different enforcement layers (edge vs service). Always apply backoff regardless. We'll also look at logs from our side for your key. Can you confirm the key id (redacted) and the project name?

Luis: key starts with pk-live-abc123, project "wordsmith-search".

Anna (support): Got it — pulling logs now.

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: embeddings-config-2026-03-15 at 03:11 UTC :rocket:

Anna (support): From our access logs: your key hit 429s starting 1852001289 — concurrent inflight peaked at ~420 requests. We show a short-term per-key limit of ~400 concurrent embedding requests. When concurrency spike > limit, the burst window drains.

Anna (support): Also noticed intermittent 400s earlier in the run — payloads with mismatched vector dims sent to our validate step. That doesn't cause 429s but can add extra retries. Can you confirm you're using the 1536-dim model (text-embedding-ada-002-v2) and not an older 1024-dim client lib?

Luis: We upgraded the client lib last week but I wasn't 100% sure on vector check. We'll verify.

Julie (eng-sre): For the backoff code, here's a small python snippet we recommend (simple, respects Retry-After):
```
import time, random

def backoff(attempt, retry_after=None):
    if retry_after:
        sleep = float(retry_after)
    else:
        sleep = min(60, (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 1))
    time.sleep(sleep)

# usage:
# attempt = 0
# while True:
#   resp = call_api()
#   if resp.status_code == 200: break
#   elif resp.status_code == 429:
#       backoff(attempt, resp.headers.get('Retry-After'))
#       attempt += 1
```

Mike (infra): Also consider client-side request coalescing: instead of 30 workers each sending small batches, have a single batching process that consumes a queue (Redis/Rabbit) and emits requests at a controlled rate. That lets you maintain throughput but avoid concurrent spikes.

Raj (billing): I checked the account plan. You're on the hosted usage plan with a default per-key burst profile; we can submit a request to expand the burst window for short-term needs, or discuss Dedicated reserved throughput for predictable SLAs. Also note that quota increases require billing review.

Luis: If we stagger and reduce concurrency, will total job time increase a lot? We need <2 hours for full run.

Julie (eng-sre): Depends. If you move to fewer workers but larger batches you might keep roughly the same token throughput. Example: 30 workers * 512 = 15360 items in parallel; switching to 6 workers * 2048 still ~12288 parallel items but fewer concurrent connections -> less chance of short-term burst throttle. But larger batches might increase per-request latency. Test locally with a synthetic run.

Anna (support): We ran a small simulation in your namespace: 30 concurrent clients x 512 batch -> 65% 429 rate within 90s. 6 clients x 2048 -> 5% 429 rate. We can share the test script if helpful. Would you like us to run a rehearsal with you in a maintenance window?

Luis: Yes please. Also, can you confirm if rate limits are per-key or per-project? Our infra spawns multiple jobs under the same key across regions.

Mike (infra): Primarily per-key, but there's also per-account and per-region soft limits to prevent cross-region storms. We'll flag your key for a one-off monitoring hook during the next run to capture more metrics.

Anna (support): Action items: 1) Luis: patch job to add exponential backoff + respect Retry-After, reduce concurrency to ~6–8 or increase batch size and stagger starts; 2) Mike/Julie: enable per-key temp monitoring hook for next run and check if we can temporarily loosen burst for this project; 3) Raj: prepare quota increase / Dedicated options and cost estimates.

Luis: On it. Please send the test script and any suggested config. Thanks for the fast turnaround. :pray:

Mike (infra): Pasting a quick repro curl loop you can run to reproduce locally (careful, it'll trigger throttles):
```
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer pk-live-abc123" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"text-embedding-ada-002-v2","input":["a","b","c", /* repeat to reach batch 512 */]}' &
done
wait
```

Julie (eng-sre): Quick FYI for the team: if the customer is regularly running big offline jobs, Dedicated pools or a private deployment with reserved GPUs will yield predictable throughput and no shared burst constraints. Worth a short call if they want to plan capacity.

Anna (support): I'll attach logs and the test script to this thread once I have the sanitized copy. Leaving a note: if you also observed dimension-related 400s in the run, double-check the embedding client post-upgrade — some wrappers changed default models/dims.

Luis: Thanks everyone — I'll try the reduced concurrency + backoff tonight and report back.

Anna (support): Great. Marking follow-up for 24 hours. If you hit anything odd, re-open this thread and we'll escalate to runtime team. :thumbsup:
